problem: The sentence 'This is why a real compression panel can be lighter than a solid sheet of the same total area' is wrong as written. A stiffened panel of the same plan area carries more material (skin plus stringers) and so is heavier; a sheet of the same material area weighs the same. The correct comparison is at equal load, not equal area.
fix: Replace with: 'This is why a stiffened panel can be lighter than an unstiffened sheet that carries the same compressive load.'

problem: The step list tells the student to limit beff to p/2, but the example never checks this limit because no pitch is given. A student may think the check is optional.
fix: Add one line: 'No pitch is given here, so the p/2 limit cannot be checked; with p = 60 mm the limit would be 30 mm per side and beff would need cutting to 30 mm.'

problem: 'if it does, the whole sheet is effective and the skin has not buckled over the full bay' is vague: the effective zones from neighbouring stringers meet, and the applied stress is at or below the local buckling stress, so the whole bay p is counted.
fix: Rewrite: 'if beff exceeds p/2, the effective zones from adjacent stringers meet; then count the whole bay width p as effective, because the applied stress is no higher than the local buckling stress of the skin.'
